newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine eyes surging wheat,barley output.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine eyes surging wheat,barley output.

text.p: KIEV, July 4 - Ukrainian wheat supply in the 1997/98 July/June season is set to soar 49 percent from 1996/97 levels, with barley jumping 41 percent and sunseeds 25 percent over the corresponding period.

Wheat output is set to surge 55 percent to 21 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 13.55 million in 1996/97. Barley production is seen growing 41 percent to 8.1 million tonnes in 1997/98, and sunseeds output to rise 32 percent year-on-year to 2.8 million.
Wheat imports are expected to fall, while barley imports should remain stable.

Rising grain supply is likely to boost feed availability, particularly taking into account the continued decline in livestock inventories. Compound feed production is likely to increase, accompanied by a corresponding price fall.

Total grain exports are forecast at 2.2-2.5 million tonnes, mostly going to coutries outside the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). Railway and the Black Sea port facilities are not able to handle bigger quantities.

In the new season, Ukrainian producers may face grain marketing problem for the first time in this country. Urgent measures are requested from the government to promote the Ukrainian grain exports mainly to Russia and other former Soviet Union countries.

The 1997/98 season's market will be very much a buyers' market for feed wheat and barley as producer grain prices are likely to be depressed. Producer sunseed stocks will be high next season (October 1-September 30).
A considerable increase in domestic crushing is expected as sunseed exports are unlikely to exceed 1.1 million tonnes in 1997/98. TABLE 1. WHEAT BALANCE, JULY 1-JUNE 30 (1,000 TONNES)
